findings.reason: the followup is what a coordinator reads to choose the next wave, so as written it under-dispatches three implementable sections and the plan would sit half-built with every section still declared implementable.
findings.text: the followup `f-aprteiig-001` is titled "Build §2, then §4" and its body accounts only for those two sections, while `plan-section-declarations` marks §5, §6 and §7 `implementable` and none of them is mentioned; a coordinator scheduling from the followup would dispatch two of the four buildable sections and leave §5's shared matching rule, §6's release repair and §7's receipt check unbuilt, even though §7's declared wait on §4 is satisfied by the same wave

findings.reason: a descope that names a section which does not cover the defect drops one of the three defects the plan's own §1 table says it exists to repair, and no later node will notice the gap.
findings.text: §3 is descoped with the reason "Duplicates a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers §4, which already owns promoting a review run on its stored record", but that section's actual deliverable is that promotion "does not require the manifest's `tests` line to be an executable command" and its done-when tests a prose `tests` line plus a missing record; it never mentions `exit_status`, `log_digest`, `gate_check` or `_default_gate_evidence_from_manifest`, which are exactly the fields §1 row 2 records as missing, so the defect §3 exists to repair is owned by nothing

findings.reason: each drifted anchor also names its file and symbol, so a worker greps the symbol and lands on the right site; the drift costs minutes and misleads no repair.
findings.text: the §5 negative-control site is cited as `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py` "near lines 2071–2097 —, where `added = control_ids - reference_ids`", but that comparison is at line 2142 (`added = [] if reference_ids is None else sorted(control_ids - reference_ids)`) and lines 2071–2097 hold the negative-control exemption branch, not the comparison; the same drift appears at §2's `canonical_node_id` ("near line 1938", actual 2002), §5's `reckon/crew/promotion_records.py` "near line 685" (the `ledger.added_failure_ids` call is at 788) and §3's `_default_gate_evidence_from_manifest` "near line 244" (actual 308)

findings.reason: the specification states the return in the same sentence the name appears in, so no implementer can read it the other way; a rename is a nicety, not a repair.

findings.reason: the per-site positive cases assert the new behaviour, so reverting either uncontrolled site fails the test suite directly; the control count is thin evidence rather than a hole a worker could fall through.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — every file and symbol an anchor names resolves (`canonical_node_id`, `_zero_added_against_a_red_base`, `_require_verdict_matches_exit_status`, `_require_gate_evidence`, `_revision_is_ancestor`, `_record_release_on_ledger`, `_release_after_promotion`, `_release_run_workspace`, `_land_a_promoted_run`, `gate_log_failure_ids`, `added_failure_ids`, the merge `commit` field, `tests/test_a_short_commit_list_is_reported.py`, the power_convertor note and the sibling plan `a-review-gate-judges-what-it-covers` all exist), but several cited line numbers have drifted.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — every node names at least one negative control that restores base behaviour (§2 exact-id compare and bracket-strip, §4 per-sha requirement, §5 restored set difference, §6 pre-merge receipt and recorded-checkout HEAD, §7 eight mutations), but §4's third case cannot distinguish its new rule from the old one.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §6 requires every log under the run directory with revision, literal command and a terminal `EXIT=`, and §7's evidence is likewise the gate log a promotion cites; §2, §4 and §5 rest on the run record's own gate and suite arms, which live in the crew run directory rather than a scratch tree.
rubric_items.naming: a finding — the symbol names and test filenames are mechanism-named with no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags, but `failure_ids_covered` is named for the opposite of its stated return.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2, §4, §6 and §7 each state a root cause the cited code supports, but §3's descope rests on a sibling plan section that does not own the defect §3 describes.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 (one predicate in one identity module), §4 (one coverage rule at one site), §5 (one matching rule across three named comparison sites), §6 (one release-accounting defect), §7 (one receipt-versus-log agreement check) each name a single deliverable; §3 is descoped, not carried alongside another goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the section relationship graph is correct (s4→s2, s5→s2, s7→s4 all resolve, and s2's predicate is the transitive input s7 needs through s4), but the plan's next-invocation followup `f-aprteiig-001` schedules only §2 and §4 while §5, §6 and §7 are declared `implementable`.
